- If sentiment is consistently low or neutral (0.00–0.20) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in subsequent periods.  
- When sentiment shows early positive signals (e.g., 0.20–0.40), model often underreacts; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with sentiment momentum.  
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early periods (e.g., 1–3 days after spike), but fails to capture longer-term trend; extend mean reversion window to 7–10 days for 30d forecasts.  
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after a high, model often fails to recognize it; add a 1–2 day lag correction to prevent premature recovery.  
- For sentiment history with no clear trend (all 0.00), model tends to forecast flat or upward; introduce a 1–2% downward bias to reflect lack of sentiment-driven momentum.
